newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Budapest BUX hits new high, ends at 3,574.65 pts.
newsitem.headline: Budapest BUX hits new high, ends at 3,574.65 pts.

text.p: Hungarian share prices surged across the board on the Budapest Stock Exchange on Monday pushing the BUX index to the second successive record high.
But traders acknowledged they did not see any immediate fundamental reasons to justify the pace of trhe rise.
The BUX index closed at 3,574.65 points, up 100.71 points. BUX index futures ended higher for four maturities and remained steady for two.
Spot share turnover totalled 1.88 billion forints as it was boosted by a block deal for 360,000 chemical company TVK shares which changed hands at 1,350 forints/share price.
Some traders referred to market talk that the Hungarian share market is still undervalued despite the fact that the BUX index more than doubled this year.

"The only reason by which I can explain is that Hungarian shares are generally undervalued compared to other European shares," Agnes Haszon of Equilor Rt said. "This can be a reason which weighs heavily."
On Monday a number of shares rose to new highs, including all shares in the pharmaceutical sector, but there were traders who said the overheated market vulnerable.
"The whole is very fragile," said Balazs Szabo of Eastbrokers.
"Two things may now happen, either the market plunges or it continues to strengthen with brief pauses," Szabo said. "But I don't see reason for a plunge as the supply side is weak."
Szabo said most companies have strong fundamentals, encouraging investors to hold the papers on the long-term.
